events.title: Rock-ice avalanche, Lirung massif
events.detail: Seismic signal 02:52:10 UTC; USGS classes it as a landslide, M5.2 (ms_vx). The map times everything from this signal; the exact moment the failure began is not known from it

events.title: Rasuwagadhi gauge: last report
events.detail: 1.62 m at 08:40; next report absent by 08:50

events.title: Gyirong Port hit (surveillance camera)
events.detail: Port surveillance video at 10:59 Beijing time (08:44 NPT), after ~22 km and ~3,400 m of descent (Guo et al. 2026); CHWRR gives the same time

events.title: Syabrubesi gauge: last report
events.detail: 3.80 m at 08:50; next report absent by 09:00

events.title: Large flood from China reported
events.detail: Rasuwa District Administration and Betrawati station staff report it; the Flood Forecasting Warning Centre receives first information at 09:05

events.title: SMS warnings sent
events.detail: About 678,295 messages between 09:05 and 09:14 (CHWRR text); its chronology table and the RDNA list the warning at 09:15, and the RDNA gives 679,295. Receipt not verified

events.title: Betrawati gauge: last report
events.detail: 3.55 m at 09:20 (warning 4.1 m); next report absent by 09:30

events.title: Flood reported at Galchhi; downstream forecast issued
events.detail: CHWRR: the wave reached the Galchhi area and was expected to cross Mugling within hours; warnings issued for the Prithvi Highway and Mugling–Narayanghat road

events.title: Galchhi gauge starts rising
events.detail: Onset 10:20–10:30; above warning by 10:40; peak 10:50, ~8.8 m above its pre-event level

events.title: Malekhu (Phurke): flood wave arrives
events.detail: Gauge rises 3.35 m → 3.96 m between 11:10 and 11:20, then crosses warning (7.0 m) between 11:20 and 11:30 (7.78 m); CHWRR reports 11:26

events.title: Phurke: above danger level; station and bridge lost (reported)
events.detail: Above danger (8.0 m) between 11:30 and 11:40; last transmitted reading 10.48 m at 11:40, none after (BIPAD). CHWRR reports 11:43

events.title: Second landslide-classified seismic signal
events.detail: 06:00:35 UTC; USGS landslide classification, M4.2 (ms_vx); location approximate. No second downstream flood is implied

events.title: Reported past Mugling by 13:00
events.detail: CHWRR: the wave crossed Mugling, and warnings went out as far as Devghat. The map's interpolated arrival here is ~13:07, a few minutes later; the Kali Khola gauge 3 km downstream (onset 13:10–13:20) is consistent with either. The map follows the gauge windows

events.title: Kali Khola gauge starts rising
events.detail: Onset 13:10–13:20; above warning 14:00; peak 12.35 m at 14:20 (danger level 12.1 m)

events.title: Devghat gauge starts rising
events.detail: Onset 14:30–14:40 in the instrument record. CHWRR is not consistent: its Table 2 logs 4.76 m at 13:20, with the main wave expected around 15:30, and the wave reaching Devghat at 15:20, while its Table 3 calls 13:20 the initial flood arrival. The map uses the gauge record

events.title: Devghat peaks at 6.57 m (stage)
events.detail: Below its 7.3 m warning level. Rating-curve estimates (CHWRR): ~5,850 m³/s; ~20 million m³ above baseline

events.title: International Charter activated
events.detail: 14:58 UTC+2 per the Charter record; requested by DHM

story.title: The collapse
story.text: Roughly 100 million m³ of rock and glacier ice breaks off the Lirung massif at ~5,150–5,200 m and drops ~1.2–1.4 km into the valley (figures differ between studies). Seismometers record a landslide-classified signal at 08:37, which the map uses as its time reference; the exact moment the failure began cannot be read from it.

story.title: A debris flow forms
story.text: The falling mass becomes a debris flow, a fast slurry of mud, rock, ice and water. It scours loose glacial debris from the valley floor and may entrain buried ice. By about 4,000 m it has mixed with river water and sediment as it moves down the narrow Lende Khola gorge.

story.title: The border crossing is hit
story.text: The port's surveillance camera shows it reaching the China–Nepal border about seven minutes after the 08:37 signal, at Gyirong Port, a busy crossing for traders and pilgrims. At the confluence it surges about 2 km upstream into China.

story.title: Almost no warning downstream
story.text: The flow enters Nepal through Timure and Syabrubesi. Xu (2026) attributes this first wave to the debris flow itself, possibly with a quick breach of debris it dumped across the river; the barrier lakes mapped on 28 August only began overflowing that afternoon. Below Syabrubesi it drops its largest boulders and becomes a more water-laden flood. River gauges stop transmitting one after another, so the timing here is bracketed rather than measured.

story.title: Warnings go out
story.text: From 09:05 emergency SMS warnings go out to six districts along the river: about 678,000 messages by 09:14 (CHWRR).

story.title: Down the Trishuli
story.text: Around Betrawati, hydropower projects, bridges and the riverside road are damaged or swept away.

story.title: A long, slower surge
story.text: Lower down the valley is wider and the flood wave travels more slowly, giving authorities time to warn towns further downstream.

story.title: Malekhu
story.text: The Malekhu gauge starts rising between 11:10 and 11:20. It passes its warning level by 11:30 and danger level by 11:40, its final transmission, and the Phurke bridge is lost.

story.title: Past Mugling
story.text: At 13:00 CHWRR reports the wave crossing Mugling. Riverside residents as far as Devghat are told to move away from the banks.

story.title: Reaching the plains
story.text: The rising wave reaches the Devghat gauge between 14:30 and 14:40 in the instrument record (reports give other times). The stage peaks at 6.57 m at 16:00, below the warning level, then falls.

story.title: What the map shows now
story.text: The shaded area is the satellite-mapped extent from the following days, revealed by estimated arrival time. Scrub the timeline or click a key event to revisit any moment.

after.title: Barrier lake warning (China MWR)
after.detail: Border lake ~2 million m³, more inflow expected

after.title: Two new barrier lakes mapped
after.detail: ~12 ha and ~19 ha (UNOSAT 4260, Cartosat-3); CHWRR gives ~16 ha and ~18 ha. Formed during the cascade

after.title: Main barrier lake starts overflowing
after.detail: 17:50 Beijing time (15:35 NPT); outflow ~50 m³/s vs inflow ~23 m³/s (China MWR, via Xu 2026)

after.title: Lake 2 overflows
after.detail: Reported downstream rises; rescues briefly paused

gauges.name: Rasuwagadhi
gauges.reading: last report 1.62 m at 08:40 (warning 6 m, danger 7 m), then lost

gauges.name: Syabrubesi
gauges.reading: last report 3.80 m at 08:50 (warning 5.5 m), then lost

gauges.name: Betrawati
gauges.reading: last report 3.55 m at 09:20 (warning 4.1 m, danger 5 m), then lost

gauges.name: Galchhi
gauges.reading: onset 10:20–10:30; peak 10:50, ~8.8 m above pre-event level

gauges.name: Phurke (Malekhu)
gauges.reading: onset 11:10–11:20; warning (7.0 m) crossed 11:20–11:30, danger (8.0 m) 11:30–11:40; last 10.48 m at 11:40, then lost (BIPAD)

lakes.name: Barrier lake 1
lakes.note: Lende–Lirung Khola confluence. Possibly the lake China's MWR surveyed by radar (~10 ha, ~2.2 million m³; dam ~60 m high, ~300 m wide; Xu 2026), but the match is not confirmed. That lake overflowed from 17:50 Beijing time (15:35 NPT) on 28 Aug. Formed during the disaster cascade; mapped on 28 Aug

lakes.name: Barrier lake 2
lakes.note: Below the collapse area; reported overflow 29 Aug. Formed during the disaster cascade; mapped on 28 Aug

rows: ~0.72 km² detached ice–rock body (Guo et al., peer reviewed); ~0.76 km² (JMS) or ~0.99 km² (JISRS), at ~5,130–5,200 m; ~2.2 km² (WWA preliminary). Each study delineated its own source area, so these are not the same outline

~103 million m³ (JMS); 99 ± 10 million m³ (JISRS); ~110 million m³ (WWA preliminary); ~132 million m³ (ICIMOD preliminary synthesis); up to ~30 million m³ more picked up on the valley floor (WWA). These are central estimates; their spread is ~99–132 million m³
M5.2 landslide signal (USGS); other agencies' magnitudes differ
14.2 km in ~350 s: a route-average rate (JMS), not a measured flow velocity
~22 km and ~3,400 m of descent to Gyirong Port; flow area ~7.3 km² (Guo et al.); becomes a debris flow by ~4,000 m
source.precursor: ICIMOD reports up to 40 cm of line-of-sight ground deformation at the source in Sentinel-1 radar between 7 Jul and 24 Aug; this is retrospective and does not imply the failure time was predictable. At the Kakani seismic station, Guo et al. find several candidate signals in the ~3 hours before (around 06:04, 06:50 and 08:15–08:19 NPT), some close to eyewitness reports of a snow avalanche and an ice-snow dust cloud. They may be small ice or rock falls, but do not establish a deterministic precursor. Sentinel-2 shows the source glacier's middle and lower parts moving relatively fast through 2024–2026.
source.rain: Satellite rainfall at the source grid cell was low before the failure (4.0 mm in 24 h, 20th percentile; 8.3 mm over 3 days), so heavy rain is not thought to be the main trigger. Local rainfall and initiation remain uncertain. The 7-day mean ERA5-Land 2 m air temperature at the source grid cell (9.43 °C) was above every matching week from 2001–2025 (Li 2026); this describes conditions, not a proven cause. Guo et al. (peer reviewed, ERA5-Land) likewise find limited rain in the final 72 hours, a warmer than average spring, and a summer up to 21 Aug +0.58 °C above average.
source.conflicts: Studies estimate geometry, volume, magnitude and speed differently; each figure is attributed to its source.

source.seen: A bare grey failure surface now replaces glacier ice on the mountain's north face, and grey debris covers the valley floor below it.
source.why: Satellite images and field photographs show that both glacier ice and rock broke away, leaving a fresh headwall and hanging ice; the detached ice–rock body covered about 0.72 km² (Guo et al.). Published central volume estimates range from about 99 to 132 million m³.
source.note: The before image is a cloud-free 2025 mosaic built from many Sentinel-2 dates at 10 m, so snow cover differs from the after image (0.6 m Pelican scene; both shown at 2.7 m per pixel): compare landforms, not snow.

videos.title: Published simulation of the first ten minutes (Movie S7)
videos.text: A rock–ice–water flow simulation (r.avaflow) on Copernicus GLO-30 terrain, starting from an imposed 200 million m³ release, larger than most volume estimates. With ice melting by friction included, the modelled flow reaches Gyirong at 457 s, close to the authors' benchmark of 458 s; the authors' runs without melting take 593 s or more. The study's paper is in preparation and not yet peer reviewed.
videos.credit: Huang, S., Chen, C.-M. & Wang, B. (2026), Movie S7, Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.22884627, CC BY 4.0. Shown unmodified.

videos.title: Upper-gorge simulation, first 24 minutes (Park)
videos.text: A 30 m rock–ice flow model from the source down to Syabrubesi, with source material starting at rest and melting that conserves mass. Flow thickness is exaggerated four times for display, and the clock converts model time to NPT. No separate temporary-dam outburst is prescribed, which the author notes does not rule one out. The run shown is the scenario the author selected; other parameter choices change the timing.
videos.credit: Park, H. (2026), Langtang 2026 rock-ice avalanche and flood: revised simulation animations and supporting outputs (v2.0.0), Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.22566624, file animation_gorge_oblique_5s.mp4, CC BY 4.0. Shown unmodified. Accompanying manuscript: preprint doi 10.31223/X5250R, not peer reviewed.

timure.seen: The riverside buildings at the Rasuwagadhi–Timure confluence are gone, and grey flood deposits fill a much wider channel.
timure.why: Here part of the flow surged about 2 km up the side valley into China, a sign it still carried great momentum at the confluence (Guo et al.; WWA). That backflow is documented but not reconstructed on this map. Copernicus EMS graded 372 building points in its Timure mapping area as destroyed, and the Rasuwagadhi gauge stopped reporting after 08:40.
timure.note: The before image is from 27 May 2026, after the July 2025 Purepu flood had already scoured this reach, so the change shown is from 2026. Cloud covers part of the after image.

videos.title: Gyirong Port camera, 26 August 2026
videos.text: A fixed surveillance camera at Gyirong Port, looking north-west (upstream), records the debris-laden surge reaching the port and engulfing the car park and buildings. Guo et al. give the port camera's time of arrival as 10:59 Beijing time (08:44 NPT); this clip's on-screen clock is not independently verified.
videos.notice: Shows the surge striking the port; people can be seen in the car park beforehand.
videos.credit: Distributed by Resound News; original camera operator unidentified. Classified as public domain on Wikimedia Commons (automated recording), accessed 9 Nov 2026. Re-encoded to MP4 without other changes.

syabrubesi.seen: Grey flood deposits now cover the low ground at the river junction where the bazaar stood, and the channel is much wider; buildings higher on the slope remain.
syabrubesi.why: WWA's narrative describes waves of 10 m to almost 100 m (a description, not a measurement) tearing through Rasuwagadhi, Timure and Syabrubesi, and the flood beginning to drop its largest rock south of Syabrubesi. Copernicus EMS graded 323 building points here as destroyed; the Syabrubesi gauge stopped reporting after 08:50.
syabrubesi.note: May (dry season) and September (monsoon) images differ in vegetation colour and hill shadow.

betrawati.seen: Muddy flood sediment now spans the valley floor; the riverside road and fields along the channel are absent or obscured.
betrawati.why: Betrawati was the first Nuwakot town the flood reached; a large share of its homes were inundated and covered in mud debris (WWA, citing national press). The Betrawati gauge stopped reporting after 09:20, and the 55 km Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi road section was completely damaged (RDNA, via WWA).
betrawati.note: Cloud hides part of the river junction in the after image.

bidur.seen: The narrow river and its canal are replaced by a broad sheet of grey sediment, and buildings close to the river are absent or obscured.
bidur.why: Downstream, the debris-laden water left mud and debris several metres thick in the market towns of Trishuli and Battar (WWA). Copernicus EMS graded 2,479 building points in its wider Bidur mapping area as destroyed.
bidur.note: The EMS count covers a mapping area larger than this 2 km view.

esa.seen: Two days before (left) the valleys are green and the glaciers cyan. About two hours after the 08:37 signal (right), ESA marks flood water and debris along the valley, partly under cloud.
esa.why: Landsat 9 passed over at 04:47 UTC (10:33 NPT), while the flood was still under way: by this map's estimate the front was then about 100 km downstream, near Galchhi. The upper corridor shown here had already been scoured.
esa.note: False colour: ice and snow appear cyan and vegetation green. These are ESA's own renderings with ESA's labels, so their framing differs from the other panels and there is no map pin.

simulations.intro: Published computer simulations of the cascade by other researchers, shown with their authors' own caveats. They are models, not footage, and their timings are independent of this map's evidence-based timeline: neither confirms the other. Each clip shows one run its authors selected; other parameter choices change the timing.

videos.title: Full-corridor simulation, 8 hours, plan view (Park)
videos.text: A 60 m two-dimensional model of the flow from the source to Devghat over eight hours, including settling and melting. The author states it is not a validated inundation map.
videos.credit: Park, H. (2026), Langtang 2026 rock-ice avalanche and flood: revised simulation animations and supporting outputs (v2.0.0), Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.22566624, file animation_full_corridor_top_60s.mp4, CC BY 4.0. Shown unmodified. Accompanying manuscript: preprint doi 10.31223/X5250R, not peer reviewed.

videos.title: Full-corridor simulation, 8 hours, long profile (Park)
videos.text: The wave travelling down the river's long profile. Below Syabrubesi this view uses a separate one-dimensional routing model fitted to the Galchhi, Kali Khola and Devghat gauges, so it differs from the plan view. Flow depth is exaggerated 50 times; the lower panel shows river rise in metres, capped at 10 m. The author reports that discrepancies remain at Devghat.
videos.credit: Park, H. (2026), Langtang 2026 rock-ice avalanche and flood: revised simulation animations and supporting outputs (v2.0.0), Zenodo doi 10.5281/zenodo.22566624, file animation_full_corridor_profile_60s.mp4, CC BY 4.0.
